Chapter 8 • Integrals

8.2 Integration on Manifolds

Let \((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}^\uparrow)\) be an oriented manifold with a volume form \(\Omega\), \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X}) \in \mathcal{A}^\uparrow\), \(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\), and \(\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{U}\) the open region over which \(f\) is to be integrated, with closure \(\overline{\mathcal{D}}\) compact and contained in \(\mathcal{U}\)7. The indicator function \(\iota\) of \(\mathcal{D}\) cuts \(f\) off outside the region: \(\iota f\) equals \(f\) on \(\mathcal{D}\) and vanishes outside it. The integral of \(f\) over \(\mathcal{D}\) is \begin{equation} \begin{split} \int_\mathcal{D} \Omega f &\coloneqq \int_{\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{U})} d^d\alpha \, \big( \omega_\mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \, \big( (\iota f) \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \\ &\overset{\substack{\iota \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \, = \, 1 \text{ on } \mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D}) \\ \text{and } 0 \text{ outside}}}{=} \int_{\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D})} d^d\alpha \, \big( \omega_\mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \, \big( f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) , \end{split} \tag{8.3} \end{equation} an ordinary integral over the open set \(\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D}) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d\), which is bounded since \(\overline{\mathcal{D}}\) is compact, see Figure 8.1.

This definition does not depend on the chart. Let \((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y}) \in \mathcal{A}^\uparrow\) be a second chart with \(\overline{\mathcal{D}} \subseteq \mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V}\), so that \(\int_\mathcal{D} \Omega f\) can be computed in either. The chart transition map \(\textrm{\runic ᛖ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}} = \mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1}\), \(\alpha = \textrm{\runic ᛖ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}}(\beta)\), maps \(\mathscr{Y}(\mathcal{D})\) onto \(\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D})\), since \(\mathscr{X}\big( \mathscr{Y}^{-1}( \mathscr{Y}(\mathcal{D}) ) \big) = \mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D})\), and \begin{align*} \int_\mathcal{D} \Omega f = &\int_{\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D})} d^d\alpha \, \big( \omega_\mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \, \big( f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \xlongrightarrow[d^d\alpha \, = \, d^d\beta \, |\det ( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} )(\beta)|]{\text{change of variables}} ... \\ ... = &\int_{\mathscr{Y}(\mathcal{D})} d^d\beta \, \Big| \det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)(\beta) \Big| \, \big( \omega_\mathscr{X} \circ \underbrace{\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \textrm{\runic ᛖ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}}}_{\mathscr{Y}^{-1}} \big)(\beta) \, \big( f \circ \underbrace{\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \textrm{\runic ᛖ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}}}_{\mathscr{Y}^{-1}} \big)(\beta) \xlongrightarrow[\text{at } p \, = \, \mathscr{Y}^{-1}(\beta)]{(8.1)} ... \\ ... = &\int_{\mathscr{Y}(\mathcal{D})} d^d\beta \, \underbrace{\frac{\big| \det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)(\beta) \big|}{\det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)(\beta)}}_{= \, +1 \text{ in } \mathcal{A}^\uparrow} \, \big( \omega_\mathscr{Y} \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1} \big)(\beta) \, \big( f \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1} \big)(\beta) , \end{align*} which is (8.3) in the chart \((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\). The absolute value produced by the change of variables is cancelled by the determinant carried by \(\omega_\mathscr{X}\) only up to its sign, and the orientation makes this sign \(+1\).

8.2.1 Integral over the Whole Manifold

A function that does not vanish outside a single chart domain is first cut into pieces that do. With \(\operatorname{supp} f \coloneqq \overline{\{ p \in \mathcal{M} \mid f(p) \neq 0 \}}\) the support of \(f\), outside which \(f\) vanishes, and \(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}_{a \in A}\) an open cover of \(\mathcal{M}\), a partition of unity subordinate to it is a family of smooth functions \(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n : \mathcal{M} \to [0, 1]\) such that

  1. subordinate: each \(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\) is contained in some \(\mathcal{U}_a\);

  2. locally finite: every point has a neighbourhood that meets only finitely many \(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\);

  3. sums to one: \(\sum_n \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n(p) = 1\) for all \(p \in \mathcal{M}\), a finite sum at every \(p\) by 2.

Multiplying by \(1 = \sum_n \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\) splits any \(f\) into the pieces \(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n f\), each vanishing outside a single \(\mathcal{U}_a\).

Let \((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}^\uparrow)\) be an oriented manifold with a volume form \(\Omega\), \(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\) with \(\operatorname{supp} f\) compact, and \(\{ \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \}\) a partition of unity subordinate to the cover of \(\mathcal{M}\) by the chart domains of \(\mathcal{A}^\uparrow\), with \(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n\) for a chart \((\mathcal{U}_n, \mathscr{X}_n) \in \mathcal{A}^\uparrow\)8. The integral of \(f\) over \(\mathcal{M}\) is \begin{equation} \int_\mathcal{M} \Omega f \coloneqq \sum_n \int_{\mathcal{U}_n} \Omega \, \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n f . \tag{8.4} \end{equation} Each term is defined by (8.3), with \(\mathcal{D}\) any open set containing \(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \cap \operatorname{supp} f\) with closure compact and contained in \(\mathcal{U}_n\): this set is compact, as a closed subset of the compact \(\operatorname{supp} f\), so such \(\mathcal{D}\) exist, and \(\iota \, \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n f = \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n f\) makes the value independent of the choice. Only finitely many terms are non-zero, since the compact \(\operatorname{supp} f\) is covered by finitely many of the neighbourhoods of item 2. The result does not depend on the partition of unity chosen.

7

The closure \(\overline{\mathcal{D}}\) is \(\mathcal{D}\) together with its boundary points. Its compactness makes the integral finite, and its containment in \(\mathcal{U}\) makes it an ordinary integral over a bounded region of \(\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{U})\). Without these conditions the integral may diverge (Appendix B.19).

8

Such a partition of unity exists because \(\mathcal{M}\) is Hausdorff and second countable (Chapter 3). The cover by all chart domains of \(\mathcal{A}^\uparrow\) is not locally finite, since infinitely many charts contain each point, but these two properties allow it to be refined to a cover in which every point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many of its sets, and the partition of unity is built on this refinement (Appendix B.20).
